item.description:
Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1871

Projections

  • The Projection's mode row shows what each mode set, with its next step as a button: paint back for Stabilize and paint, a dome for Sky, a 2D insert for Screen insert, the object's shape for Clean-plate removal, and cards for DMP cards.
  • DMP cards puts each layer of a layered painting (a Photoshop file, or an EXR with layers) on a card of its own inside the projection, at its depth. The panel lists the layers, with depth from their names, their order or typed, even depth or even parallax, and erode, feather and fill against fringes.
  • The hold can be a grain-free average of the frames round it, beside the Projection. Compare the averaged hold against the single frame in the Viewer.
  • The lineup strip shows whether the projection stays on the plate through the shot, with Checker, Edges and Difference views.
  • Fixed: closing a comp after removing DMP cards could crash Kento.

New

  • Matte Refine works a rough matte's edge out from the picture's colours: hair, motion blur and defocus. Two solves on a menu, frame by frame with an option to steady the matte over neighbouring frames, and the band from the matte's edge, painted, or both.
  • A gizmo's own text, dividers and buttons show on its panel where its author put them. Buttons Kento can press work; the rest are marked as imported from Nuke.

Faster

  • Renders work out a blur's input whole before the blur, so threads stop waiting on each other: a size 50 Blur renders about a third faster, and some studio comps nearly twice as fast.
  • ColorCorrect works about twice as fast and Gamma about a quarter faster; other color nodes read their pixels faster too.
  • Nodes fed only black pass black on without working it out.

Remote control

  • Assistants and scripts connected to Kento reach much more of it: node housekeeping, keys and links, Roto shapes and paint strokes, Trackers and the CameraTracker, the Projection's mode, hold, checks and next step, the Viewer's exposure, gamma and channel, playback, preferences, per-node timings and recent messages.
  • They can build several nodes and their wires in one step, as one undo, and press a node's panel buttons.
  • Commands lists everything they can do, and a mistyped name comes back with the nearest ones.
  • While a dialog is open or you're dragging, their changes wait.

Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1830

Inpaint and Generate

  • Kento > Generative > Inpaint fills a projection's baked textures. Its panel shows the takes and what they cost, the request line, Fill... and More takes..., and Again as it was.
  • Generate works the same way: a request, a price for each still, and a run in the background.
  • Generation jobs run in the Render Queue.
  • Takes has its own panel beside Shot, with In use, Working, Parked and Rejected. Drag a take between them, or double-click one to use it.
  • Compare wipes the take in use against what came in or against another take. In the Takes panel, right-click a take to compare it.
  • A Roto can be a fill's source. The sheet's brush marks what to fill, and its eraser marks what to leave alone.
  • Settings, Preferences, Generative sets where takes go and an optional spending limit for the comp.
  • Renders made from a generated take say so in the Render Queue and the Shot panel.

Projections

  • A hint under the hold row tells you when another frame would give more of the picture. Best hold... shows the shot's scores.
  • Checks show under the hint, each with its fix: a soft hold, a plane seen edge on or too thin, a bake that's out of date, lens distortion on a plate that isn't undistorted, overscan that's too short, motion blur off on a fast move, and the plate's grain frozen.
  • A face the bake never saw borrows the opposite face for now, under its own texture.
  • Extrude, Fold and Bend are on the plate tool's bar.
  • An awning can hinge off a cut-out's top, and a flap off an awning's side.

Comps from Nuke

  • IDefocus, Filler, Exponential Glow and LightWrapPro rebuild their insides when you change their controls, as they do in Nuke. Moving DasGrain's sample box sets its sample frame.
  • A gizmo's reset and set-frame buttons work in Kento. Kento keeps all its other buttons for Nuke.
  • A .nk saved from Kento keeps everything the script had: each node's scripts and help, a gizmo's panel, the Viewer's settings, hidden inputs, Dot labels and colors, backdrops, format names, and names with spaces.
  • Saved colorspaces and Write displays are kept, so the comp opens in Nuke in the same spaces.
  • Fixed: a clone could take the name of a later node.
  • Fixed: a comp with a Card wouldn't save as a .ko.

Faster

  • IDefocus renders about 100 times faster, and Glint about 20 times faster.
  • Very large blurs (a glow's) render about 25 times faster.
  • Motion-blurred transforms and trackers render 2 to 5 times faster.
  • Merges, corner pins and Roto written to rgba are faster too.
  • Comps from the studio's library, measured on a sample of them, render in about a sixth of the time they did.

Also

  • Remote control can grab a single panel, and it can run the Render Queue.
  • Scrubbing the time ruler moves the playhead, and a closed Dope Sheet no longer slows playback.

Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1756

Shapes from a matte

  • Press and hold the plate tool's shape button for From a Roto shape and From a node's alpha.
  • From a Roto shape: the shape's outline is the Roto's at the hold frame, its feather the Roto's, and it stays linked: change the Roto or the hold and it follows. Drag one of its points to make it your own.
  • From a node's alpha: the shape covers the matte's bounds and the matte is its edge, soft or hard, each projector's at its own frame.
  • On the Card panel a shape's row says what it's from; click the words to change it.

Foreground, as Tour Into the Picture's

  • A cut-out stands on the plane it touches: on a floor, hanging from a ceiling, out of a side wall. A plane square to the camera says why it can't take one.
  • A cut-out can stand on a block's top, or on a side the camera sees (a plant on a table, a sign on a crate); the on menu lists the faces the camera sees.
  • A + off each cut-out's left and right side hinges a plane there at the bar's angle (a door ajar, a bag carried).
  • The shape feather is live: Roto's, the outline solid and the picture fading past it; a hole fades its plane to its edge.

Projections

  • Projector stacks (BlendMat, MergeMat) draw more than 16 surfaces, at the same speed as before up to 16.
  • A texture a plane holds its plane's cut-outs too; Send to paint opens, beside it, a guide of where cut-outs hide the plane.

Shots

  • A dot in the shot menu marks each shot with something newer than its newest comp reads; hover to see what. The shot menu shows the code bright and the task dim.
  • Settings, Preferences, Shot panel: the provider, its folder, what each provider supports, who is signed in, and the panel's options.

Also

  • A turned or scaled Transform renders about twice as fast, the picture the same.
  • CameraTracker's Export makes a point cloud, or a camera, points and a render together.
